To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gas pockets in lateral portal images of prostate patients are associated with significant rectum and CTV shifts and that the lateral position of the ventral rectum border in these images correlates with the rectum wall shift and the anterior-posterior CTV shift.

the appearance of gas pockets in lateral portal images of prostate patients can be used to estimate the anterior-posterior position of the CTV and that the ventral edge position of gas pockets correlates significantly with the anterior posterior shift of the rectal wall.
The lateral edge of large gas pockets can be used to estimate the anterior-posterior position of the rectum and prostate, which is important for treatment of prostate cancer.

the development of a method for the quantitative analysis of lateral portal images in prostate cancer patients.
the detection of internal organ movement.
